head: 779635571ba48999068a61ae56ec1ae98678509e
title: Fixed bulk label removal changing the selected members
body:
Fixes https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/issues/32426

With members filtered by label A, removing A and B sends separate requests that each re-evaluate the filter. After A is removed, the second request no longer matches those members, so B remains despite a success notification.

Add a `removeLabels` action that selects matching member IDs once and removes the requested relations in one transaction. Preserve the existing `removeLabel` action. Core advertises `config.capabilities.membersBulkRemoveLabels`; Admin allows multiple labels only when that capability is present and keeps single-label removal with older servers. Rejections and unsuccessful responses do not show success.

Validation:
- 89 Core unit tests passed in the member repository and public-config suites (Node 22.23.4, Vitest 4.1.12, isolated sandbox, one worker).
- A separate harness using the real repository/model with SQLite reproduced the original defect and verified stable filtered selection, invalid payloads, no matches, legacy removal and rollback of all 102 relations after an injected later-chunk deletion failure.
- Added acceptance cases for capability present, absent and false, plus server rejection during a mixed rollout. These browser tests have **not run**: Chromium was absent and its download timed out twice. The new HTTP tests and config snapshot also remain unexecuted because local MySQL/Docker was unavailable. SQLite is not presented as MySQL/HTTP validation.
- Commit hooks passed formatting, Admin Framework/Admin/Core ESLint, dependency boundaries, staged-file scanning and changeset validation.
- Full `pnpm check` was not completed for this branch. The batch's check on the same source/dependency base stopped at repository-wide formatting before full lint/tests.

[Reproduction and validation details](https://github.com/JoaoMarcos44/Ghost/blob/e2433b625dc9f4776ecbf3dec55e7ca4c2f7849f/reports/ghost-prs-2026-10-31/labels/results.md) · [Visual explanation](https://github.com/JoaoMarcos44/Ghost/blob/e2433b625dc9f4776ecbf3dec55e7ca4c2f7849f/reports/ghost-prs-2026-10-31/labels/infographic_report.md)

![Removing selected labels together from one stable member selection](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JoaoMarcos44/Ghost/e2433b625dc9f4776ecbf3dec55e7ca4c2f7849f/reports/ghost-prs-2026-10-31/labels/infographic.png)

</details>

Full details: Linked Issues check
**Explanation** Issue `#32426` requires removal of all selected labels from the original filtered member set. The change adds Core `removeLabels` handling that selects matching member IDs once and deletes the selected relations in one transaction. The change preserves `removeLabel`, advertises `config.capabilities.membersBulkRemoveLabels`, and enables Admin multi-label removal only for servers with that capability. Admin tests cover one-request removal, legacy rejection, unsuccessful responses, and absent or false capability values. Core unit and repository tests cover selection, validation, relation deletion, and transaction behavior. The reported SQLite harness also verified rollback and stable selection. The unexecuted browser and MySQL/HTTP tests limit validation depth but do not establish an unmet issue requirement.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check
**Explanation** The changed API types, Admin modal and action flow, capability configuration, Core endpoint validation, member model query, repository transaction logic, and related tests directly support issue `#32426`. Compatibility handling for legacy servers and failure responses supports the required removal flow. No unrelated change is established by the supplied whole-pull-request summary.
Full details: Tooling Ownership
**Explanation** The PR changes 16 files under `apps/...` and `ghost/...` only. They contain application/API behavior and tests, including runtime public configuration and test snapshots. No changed path is under `tools`, `scripts`, `.github/scripts`, `tools/configs`, `tools/gx`, `ghost/scripts`, or `ghost/bin`; therefore the tooling ownership rules do not apply and no placement or execution problem is introduced.
Full details: Type-Safe Boundaries
**Explanation** The PR consumes new HTTP response and config data without runtime validation. `useBulkEditMembers` changes the response type to the hand-written `BulkEditResponseType`, but its request uses `createMutation` without `parseResponse`; `handleRemoveLabel` then reads `result.bulk.meta.stats.unsuccessful` at `apps/admin/src/members/components/members-actions.tsx:118-126`. The shared hook returns the raw JSON as the generic type. The PR also reads `configData.config.capabilities?.membersBulkRemoveLabels` at `apps/admin/src/members/members.tsx:402-403` without parsing the `/config/` response. The changed code therefore trusts boundary data based only on TypeScript types. **Resolution** Define Zod schemas for the new bulk-edit response and the consumed config capability, derive `BulkEditResponseType` and the relevant config type with `z.infer`, and pass the schemas through `parseResponse` for `useBulkEditMembers` and `useBrowseConfig` before consumers use the data. Keep the existing server-side request validation for `removeLabels`, and add schema coverage for any new HTTP input if the endpoint contract is represented by Zod.

The bulkDestroy call already preserves the transaction and error behavior.

Full details: Type-Safe Boundaries

Explanation

The PR consumes new HTTP response and config data without runtime validation. useBulkEditMembers changes the response type to the hand-written BulkEditResponseType, but its request uses createMutation without parseResponse; handleRemoveLabel then reads result.bulk.meta.stats.unsuccessful at apps/admin/src/members/components/members-actions.tsx:118-126. The shared hook returns the raw JSON as the generic type. The PR also reads configData.config.capabilities?.membersBulkRemoveLabels at apps/admin/src/members/members.tsx:402-403 without parsing the /config/ response. The changed code therefore trusts boundary data based only on TypeScript types.

Resolution

Define Zod schemas for the new bulk-edit response and the consumed config capability, derive BulkEditResponseType and the relevant config type with z.infer, and pass the schemas through parseResponse for useBulkEditMembers and useBrowseConfig before consumers use the data. Keep the existing server-side request validation for removeLabels, and add schema coverage for any new HTTP input if the endpoint contract is represented by Zod.
